A man from Khuza'ah said: "What is the reward for it, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No hypocrite will ever recite it, nor a man in whose heart there is doubt about Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, the angels brought near to Allah have been reciting it since Allah created the heavens and the earth, and they do not cease from reciting it. No servant recites it at night except that Allah, glorified is He, sends angels to protect him in his religion and his worldly affairs, and they supplicate Allah for his forgiveness and mercy. If he recites it by day, he is given a reward equal to what the day illuminates and the night darkens."

A man from Qays Aylan said: "Give us more of this hadith, may my father and mother be ransomed for you, O Messenger of Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Learn ﴿About what do they question one another?﴾ [Surah al-Naba' 1], and learn ﴿Qaf. By the glorious Qur'an﴾ [Surah Qaf 1], and learn ﴿By the sky with its constellations﴾ [Surah al-Buruj 1], and learn ﴿By the sky and the night-comer﴾ [Surah al-Tariq 1]. If you knew what is in them, you would neglect what you are engaged in, and you would learn them and draw near to Allah, glorified is He, through them. [Source: Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/411.]

Al-Khabbazi told me, saying: Zafran told us, saying: Ibn Abi Dawud told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Asim told us, saying: Shababah ibn Sawwar told us, saying: Mukhallad ibn Abd al-Wahid told us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Zirr, from Ubayy, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the surah ﴿Those who disbelieved﴾ will be on the Day of Resurrection with the best of creation, whether traveling or resident."

[Source: Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/411.]

Al-Husayn told me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali told us, saying: Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Abd Rabbih told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, saying: I heard Qatadah narrating from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded me to recite to you ﴿Those who disbelieved﴾." ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.﴾

﴿until the clear proof came to them﴾: the clear proof, the evident argument, is Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿reciting pure scriptures﴾, that is, reading them, free from falsehood. ﴿Within them are upright scriptures﴾, that is, straight and just books from Allah. ﴿And those given the Scripture did not divide except after the clear proof had come to them﴾, that is, they divided concerning the affair of Muhammad (ﷺ) and denied him. The clear proof is the explanation in their books that he is a prophet sent.

The scholars said: From the beginning of the surah up to His saying ﴿within them are upright scriptures﴾, its ruling concerns those among the People of the Book and the polytheists who believed. ﴿And they did not divide﴾ concerns those among the People of the Book who did not believe after the proofs were established against them.

Some of the imams of lexicography said: His saying "munfakkīn" means "perishing," from the phrase "infakka sulā al-mar'ah" (the woman's pelvic joint separated at childbirth) when it separates and does not heal, and so she perishes. The meaning of the verse is: they were not perishing, that is, not punished, except after the proof was established against them by the sending of the Messenger and the revelation of the books.

Al-A'mash read "wa-l-mushrikūn" in the nominative. In the codex of Abd Allah it reads: "Lam yakun al-mushrikūn wa-ahl al-kitāb munfakkīn." In the reading of Ubayy it reads: "Mā kāna alladhīna kafarū min ahl al-kitāb wa-l-mushrikīn munfakkīn ḥattā ta'tīhim al-bayyinah rasūlan min Allah," in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (qat' and ḥāl).

﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾: that is, these disbelievers were not commanded except that they worship Allah sincerely in religion, meaning in tawhid (affirming Allah's oneness) and obedience ﴿upright﴾, inclining away from all other religions to the religion of Islam.

Ibn Abbas said: "ḥunafā'" means pilgrims. Qatadah said: al-ḥanifiyyah is circumcision, the prohibition of marrying mothers, daughters, sisters, paternal aunts and maternal aunts, and performing the rites of pilgrimage.

Sa'id ibn Hamzah said: The Arabs do not call anyone ḥanīf except one who has performed the pilgrimage and been circumcised. ﴿And establish prayer and give zakah﴾, ﴿and that is the upright religion﴾, that is, the straight religion that you have mentioned. He attributed "religion" to "upright" (qayyimah), which is an instance where the two wordings differ, and he made "upright" feminine because he referred it back to the faith and the law. It was said that the ha' in it is for emphasis (al-mubalaghah).

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hanbali say: I heard Abu Sahl Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Ash'ath al-Taliqani say: The "upright" here refers to the scriptures that have been mentioned, and "religion" is attributed to them in the sense: ﴿and that is the religion of the upright scriptures﴾ in what they call to and command. A parallel is His saying: ﴿And He sent down with them the Book in truth, to judge between people concerning that over which they differed﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah 213].

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: I asked al-Khalil ibn Ahmad about His saying ﴿and that is the religion of the upright﴾, and he said: "al-qayyimah" is the plural of "al-qayyim," and "al-qayyim" [and "al-qa'im"] is singular. The sense of the verse is: and that is the religion of those who uphold tawhid for you.

[Source: Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/414.]

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding therein eternally. Those are the worst of creation﴾: al-bariyyah means creation. Nafi' read "al-bari'ah" with a hamzah in both places, and similarly Ibn Dhakwan reported from the people of Syria, following the original form, since it comes from their saying: "Barra'a Allah al-khalq yabra'uhum bar'an" (Allah created the creatures). Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿before We bring it into being﴾ [Surah al-Hadid 22]. The others read it with shaddah and without hamzah. It has two possible explanations:

The first: he dropped the hamzah and introduced the shaddah in its place.

The second: that it is fa'ilah from al-bara', which is dust. The Arabs say: "Bi-fika al-bara'" (dust in your mouth). Its meaning: those created from dust.

﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, those are the best of creation. Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is for whoever fears his Lord.﴾

Al-Sadiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "By what had preceded for them of care and success, and they were pleased with Him by what He bestowed upon them of following His Messenger and accepting what came to them with." That is, the clarification of the creatures' pleasure with Allah is their being pleased with what descends upon them of His rulings, and His pleasure with them is that He grants them success in being pleased with Him.

Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl said: Rest and comfort lie in contentment and certainty. Contentment is the greatest gate of Allah and the resting place of worshippers. Muhammad ibn Haqiq said: Contentment divides into two kinds: contentment with Him and contentment with what He does. Contentment with Him is being content with Him as Lord and Disposer, and contentment with Him in what He decrees and ordains.

It was said: Contentment is the removal of choice. Dhu al-Nun said: Contentment is the joy of the heart in the bitterness of the decree. Harith said: Contentment is the tranquility of the heart under the flow of the judgment. Abu Amr al-Dimashqi said: Contentment is the end of patience. Abu Bakr ibn Tahir said: Contentment is the removal of aversion from the heart until there remains only joy and happiness. Al-Wasiti said: It is looking at things in a way that nothing angers you except what angers your Master. Ibn Ata' said: It is looking at the ancient kindness of Allah to the servant, so that one abandons anger toward Him.

I heard Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Muhammad say: I heard Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim say: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Husayn say: I heard Ali ibn Abd al-Hamid say: I heard al-Sahmi say: If you are not pleased with Allah, how can you ask Him to be pleased with you?
